subject: Privacy & Digital Rights
title: The Eternal Arms Race
description: A fast breakdown of The Eternal Arms Race for builders.

hook.text: Every cipher ever created was eventually broken — except the ones that haven't been. Yet.

buildup.text: Cryptography is a permanent arms race between code makers and code breakers stretching back millennia.

discovery.text: Each breakthrough in breaking codes drives innovation in making stronger ones. The cycle never stops.

twist.text: AI, quantum computing, and new mathematics will change the battlefield, but not the fundamental contest.

climax.text: Encryption is never finished. It's a living science that must evolve faster than the threats against it.

punchline.text: Codes are made. Codes are broken. Forever.

quiz.question: Why is cryptography described as an 'arms race'?
options: Each breakthrough in breaking codes drives creation of stronger ones
Militaries are the only users of encryption
New ciphers are developed every week
